The prime minister has been charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in three complex and overlapping criminal cases that hinge on his relationship with telecoms magnates and other wealthy businessmen. Ending the trial without a ruling could set damaging precedents for media independence and how politicians are held to account.

events.title: Israeli strikes kill 16 schoolchildren so far this month, Gaza ministry says
events.summary:
Statement follows death of sisters, aged 15 and 13, in airstrike on residential apartment in Gaza City

Israeli strikes have killed at least 16 schoolchildren in Gaza since the start of November, as young people across the territory face intensifying bombardment and a struggle to find food, clean water and shelter.

On Wednesday, Gaza’s ministry of education said: “Palestinian students had been targeted for the third time in less than 24 hours, in an escalation reflecting the continued Israeli violations against children in the Gaza Strip. The number of schoolchildren killed since the beginning of November has now risen to 16.”

Continue reading...

events.title: Israel ‘officially sanctions’ torture of Palestinian prisoners to extract confessions, report concludes
events.summary:
Public Committee Against Torture in Israel examined 42 complaints against Shin Bet interrogators over past decade

Israel has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinian prisoners, sometimes documenting abuse in official records or granting advanced approval for “special measures” in interrogation, according to a report from the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI).

This dangerous practice risked leading to irreversible miscarriages of justice, as Israel moved to implement a racist new death penalty law that targets Palestinians, the report said.

Continue reading...

events.title: UN sacked Palestinian staff on back of unproven Israeli allegations, tribunal rules
events.summary:
Judgment casts doubt on evidence linking aid workers to Hamas and says humanitarian efforts in Gaza were damaged

A UN tribunal has cast doubt on the evidence used to justify the sacking of Palestinian UN aid workers in 2024, saying it was based “almost entirely” on unproven assertions from the Israeli government and had damaged humanitarian operations in Gaza.

The judgment, seen by the Guardian, raises fresh questions about the decision by the UN Relief and Works Agency (Unrwa), the main humanitarian organisation working in Gaza, to sack members of staff. It was taken on the basis of Israeli allegations of involvement in the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023.

Continue reading...

events.title: Palestinian journalist killed by Israel in Gaza wins Rory Peck prize
events.summary:
Mariam Dagga shares award with two of her colleagues from AP for ‘powerful coverage’ of human cost of war

Mariam Dagga, the Palestinian war correspondent who was killed at the age of 33 in Gaza in an Israeli strike, has posthumously won the prestigious Rory Peck prize for freelance video journalists, the organisers announced on Wednesday.

She shares the award with two of her colleagues from the Associated Press (AP), Abdel Kareem Hana and Jehad Alshrafi, “for their powerful coverage of the human cost of the war” in the Palestinian territory, the Rory Peck Trust said.

Continue reading...

events.title: Oxford museum displays seized belongings of Naga freedom fighter Gaidinliu for first time
events.summary:
Notebooks, clothes and ritual objects taken by British forces in India in the 1930s go on show at Pitt Rivers Museum

In 1932, British forces in north-east India imprisoned a 17-year-old girl called Gaidinliu for leading an uprising against colonial rule. While pursuing the freedom fighter through hills and valleys in the homeland of the Naga people, colonial officers also seized some of her most treasured possessions.

They were sent to the University of Oxford’s Pitt Rivers Museum and kept in storage. Now, for the first time, the museum is exhibiting the collection of 27 items, including a basket of Gaidinliu’s notebooks believed to contain her prophetic visions as the leader of a Naga Indigenous religion, clothes, bracelets and amulets.

Continue reading...

events.title: Politician hosts 400,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state
events.summary:
Six helipads built and feast prepared by 500 cooks for wedding hosted by Anant Singh, a politician charged with murder

It takes a brave soul to try to match the mythic opulence of the wedding arranged by the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani for his son Anant in 2024. Estimates of the cost for the months-long celebration ran to at least $600m, with world leaders and celebrities among those on the guest list.

Smaller fry though he is, Anant Singh, a legislator in India’s poorest state, Bihar, gave it his best shot on Wednesday, albeit in a rustic rural setting, for the nuptials of his daughter Shivangi Singh, and Rishikesh Kumar, an MBA student from Georgia State University in Atlanta.

Continue reading...

events.title: Indian Cockroach movement leader asks court for permission to fly to UK
events.summary:
Officials at Delhi airport stopped Saurav Das from boarding flight to Britain, where students have invited him to speak

A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has asked the Delhi high court to give him permission to fly to the UK after immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him boarding a flight early on Tuesday morning.

The court is scheduled to hear Saurav Das’s case on Thursday morning. His lawyer asked the court for a quick hearing because Das has by now already missed some of his engagements at British universities and can only attend the other events on his itinerary if he is allowed to fly out as soon as possible.

Continue reading...

events.title: World Chess Championship 2026 Game 1: Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov play to 38-move draw – as it happened
events.summary:
• Sindarov and Gukesh play to 38-move draw in Game 1

  • Explainer: all your pre-match questions, answered

  • Sindarov interview: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’

  • Play through 22 famous world championship games

The players have shaken hands and we’re off! We have a Berlin defense of the Ruy Lopez (1 e4 e5 2 Nf3 Nc6 3 Bb5 Nf6), one of the most thoroughly analyzed openings in modern chess.

The Berlin famously helped Vladimir Kramnik dethrone Garry Kasparov in their 2000 world title match in London and has been a staple of elite chess ever since, earning a reputation as one of black’s most reliable weapons against 1 e4.

Continue reading...

events.title: Leader of India’s Cockroach movement says he was stopped from boarding flight to UK
events.summary:
Saurav Das was due to give talks at UK universities on protest movement but says ‘coward government’ prevented him flying

A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has said he was prevented from leaving Delhi to fly to the UK to give talks on the viral group’s protests.

Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May. Das, who was due to fly out early on Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged.

Continue reading...

events.title: DWP cyber incident ‘probably an attack’, says former UK chief technology officer
events.summary:
Government took down pensions and benefits portal on Thursday but said regular payments will not be affected

A serious cyber incident that forced ministers to take down online benefits and pension services was “probably an attack”, the UK’s former chief technology officer has said.

The Department for Work and Pensions took down several systems that appeared to still be offline on Saturday morning. David Knott, who led government technology until December 2025, said much infrastructure was outdated, and underinvestment in defence and increasing sophistication of attacks meant it was only getting more vulnerable.

Continue reading...

events.title: Woman ‘traumatised’ by Sainsbury’s shoplifting ban after staff facial recognition error
events.summary:
Monia Indge, 58, who has terminal cancer, escorted from supermarket after staff using FaceWatch technology misidentified her

A woman with terminal cancer has been left “traumatised and violated” after being falsely accused of shoplifting and banned from Sainsbury’s by staff using facial recognition technology.

Monia Indge, 58, was shopping with her husband in the Walters Yard branch of Sainsbury’s in Bromley on 7 November when she was suddenly told to leave by a member of staff who told her she was “banned for life” from the store.

Continue reading...

events.title: Unpaid TV licence or cycling on pavement could bar people from settling in UK
events.summary:
Exclusive: New immigration rules will introduce strict threshold where any adult conviction triggers mandatory refusal

People could be barred from settling in the UK over minor infractions such as cycling on the pavement or failing to pay a TV licence, ministers have been warned before the introduction of new “earned settlement” rules.

Under the plans, which are to come into effect next year, securing indefinite leave to remain will become significantly harder for many people. The rules introduce a strict new threshold where any adult conviction resulting in a court disposal – including fines, community orders, conditional cautions, and absolute or conditional discharges – triggers mandatory refusal.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘I told it to never call me again’: AI bots wreak havoc with UK restaurant bookings
events.summary:
Meta claims its Muse assistant will make users’ lives easier, but business owners say AI is driving them to go analogue

Restaurant owners are battling a horde of AI bots and returning to using the telephone instead of online booking as new virtual assistants launch in the UK – but sometimes even that isn’t enough to stop them.

This week, Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta launched its Muse AI assistant in the UK and is encouraging users to let it shop and make restaurant reservations. The bot is given access to the user’s email if they give it permission, and it can make restaurant bookings and go shopping on the user’s behalf.

Continue reading...

events.title: Mental health patients refusing NHS treatment over shared therapy notes
events.summary:
Exclusive: Uploading of intimate psychiatric information to wider medical records prompts some to shun support altogether

Some psychiatric patients are refusing treatment over the NHS adding intimate details from therapy sessions to their medical notes, fuelling fears that breaching privacy is posing a risk to health, the Guardian can reveal.

One stopped medical care for a heart condition when he discovered that details of intrusive sexual thoughts he’d experienced as result of obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) had been shared with a cardiac nurse.

Continue reading...

events.title: Purse found of woman, 24, swept from California beach three weeks ago
events.summary:
Se Nah Park was overwhelmed by a wave at the notorious Panther Beach

The purse of a 24-year-old who was swept into the ocean at a notorious California beach three weeks ago was found on Wednesday, as the west coast saw record high king tides.

The Santa Cruz county sheriff’s office confirmed that Se Nah Park’s purse was found by a beachgoer at 4 Mile Beach, south of Panther Beach, where she was swept away into the ocean on 8 November.

Continue reading...

events.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for allegedly stealing trade secrets
events.summary:
Lawsuit also alleging pressure on hardware suppliers comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching employees

OpenAI sued Apple on Friday, accusing the company of ⁠stealing its trade secrets ​and discouraging hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices.

The suit, filed in northern California federal court, comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology.

Continue reading...

events.title: Thousands still without power after storms that snarled Thanksgiving travel
events.summary:
Heavy rains and high winds downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia

Skies cleared along the US eastern seaboard on Friday, and power was being restored to hundreds of thousands of customers whose Thanksgiving plans were disrupted by heavy rains and high winds that swept over the region a day earlier.

The storms snarled travel, downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia. At its peak, nearly a million customers were without power.

Continue reading...

events.title: Sales for Biden memoir fall far short of books by Obama and Clinton
events.summary:
Promise Me, America, which has lukewarm reviews from critics, sold about 21,000 copies during its first week on sale

Joe Biden’s memoir Promise Me, America debuted with modest sales and lackluster reviews, selling about 21,000 copies during its first week on sale, according to Circana.

It sold well enough to top the New York Times nonfiction bestseller list, but didn’t approach the level of memoirs by such predecessors as Barack Obama and Bill Clinton.

Continue reading...

events.title: Newly released documents suggest CIA did more post-9/11 waterboarding than previously acknowledged
events.summary:
Declassified documents appear to support belief that waterboarding was more common and may have occurred beyond two acknowledged sites

Newly released documents suggest that the CIA waterboarded more detainees during the post-9/11 “war on terror” than previously acknowledged, utilizing a site north of Kabul, Afghanistan, for the practice of simulated drowning.

The agency has acknowledged waterboarding three men: Abu Zubaydah, believed to be a high-ranking member of al-Qaida; Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, suspected architect of the 11 September 2001 attacks; and Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri, accused of planning the 2000 bombing of a navy destroyer.

Continue reading...

events.title: Sudan's lost generation: War is stealing the childhood of millions
events.summary: Three years of war have stolen childhood from millions of children in Sudan, leaving them displaced, hungry and fighting for survival instead of learning in a classroom.

events.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
events.summary: The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.

events.title: As UN Secretary General's last day approaches, search for his replacement continues
events.summary: The UN Secretary General's term ends this year, but the big powers at the UN have been unable to agree on a replacement. UN watchers worry that there will be little time to get up to speed.

events.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and deputy secretary of state, has died
events.summary: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80.

events.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
events.summary: As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease.

events.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
events.summary: Leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the U.S. and South Korea.

events.title: Storms disrupt Thanksgiving travel. And, FCC violated ABC's free speech, judge says
events.summary: The East Coast's weather is a major concern this holiday, as it could lead to coastal flooding. And, the judge says the FCC can't punish ABC for satire Trump doesn't like.

events.title: How American Thanksgiving took root — and evolved — in Liberia
events.summary: The first settlers of Liberia were African Americans who brought along the holiday of Thanksgiving — which has evolved to reflect the history and identity of this new nation.

events.title: Army to detonate tons of lead azide after delays. And, Abrego Garcia leaves U.S.
events.summary: Authorities have evacuated a 5-mile radius to prepare to dispose of thousands of pounds of lead azide. And, after a nearly two-year legal battle, Kilmar Abrego Garcia's has voluntarily left the U.S.

events.title: Republican wants FBI and CIA answers before questioning Nvidia chief
events.summary: "The public is rightly concerned," says the Republican lawmaker, who wants to know what the FBI and CIA knew about potential national security threats and whether Jensen Huang was warned.

events.title: As Spain votes, what could change for Europe?
events.summary: Spain votes on Sunday. A loss for Pedro Sanchez and a shift to the right in Madrid could affect how one of the EU's largest countries approaches migration, defense and the war in Gaza.

events.title: Germany news: Job market unlikely to recover before summer
events.summary: The head of Germany's employment agency said employment would remain at its current level for a while. Meanwhile, electric vehicle sales are expected to pass 1 million next year. DW has more.

events.title: Afghanistan: Several killed in blast near middle school
events.summary: Officials have said improperly stored explosives at a mining site ignited, damaging nearby buildings including a school. An investigation is ongoing.

events.title: India: Hindu lamp lighting at disputed Thiruparankundram pillar today
events.summary: The Supreme Court has directed that the Tamil Hindu ceremonial Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit today at the disputed Deepathoon pillar. DW has the latest.

events.title: Indian workers fill Germany's labor gaps but face hurdles and risks
events.summary: The number of Indians working in Germany has grown rapidly in recent years. But many continue to face challenges in the labor market. Some also fall victim to recruitment scams, leaving them vulnerable to exploitation.

events.title: Polls close in Taiwan's closely watched local elections
events.summary: While campaigners have stayed away from the topic of China and focused on issues like transport and childcare, Beijing is putting pressure on the progressive candidate for Taipei mayor.

events.title: Spain's Sanchez makes final appeal to voters before election
events.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez told people to turn out in large numbers so the country does not go "backwards." Polls suggest an end to his eight-year leftist leadership of Spain.

events.title: US disables ship in Gulf of Oman under Iran blockade
events.summary: The United States said it was continuing "to strictly enforce the blockade" of Iran's ports. Meanwhile, Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador over a strike that killed two Italian technicians.

events.title: Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill
events.summary: Quebec's government passed Bill 21 to ban religious symbols for public servants, arguing it was necessary to protect its secularist society. Critics argue the bill weakens legal protections for fundamental rights.

events.title: Germany news: Lawmakers approve debt-laden 2027 budget
events.summary: German lawmakers voted on a federal budget which foresees €556 billion in spending. Elsewhere, the Left Party is hosting a summit on femicide and the BSW party conference starts in Dresden. DW has more.

events.title: Spanish rider Marc Marquez announces MotoGP retirement, days after clinching record 8th world title
events.summary: Marc Marquez took fans and his team by surprise when announcing this weekend's race in Valencia will be his last. The 33-year-old won a record eight MotoGP titles, including his rookie and retirement seasons.

events.title: France seeks German man in Channel migrant boat probe
events.summary: A German businessman is accused of supplying equipment to smugglers organizing migrant crossings from France to the United Kingdom. However, he can't face formal charges until he is extradited to France.

events.title: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit
events.summary: An EU leaders summit on the bloc's seven-year budget fell apart amid divisions over how to fund Ukraine. The budget proposal also includes a 3% tax on US tech companies, in a bid for the EU to generate additional funds.

events.title: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, Brussels' most anticipated new art museum, opens its doors
events.summary: A major addition to Europe's cultural scene: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, the new contemporary art museum in a former Citroen factory complex, is celebrating its opening with a free, nonstop weekend program.

events.title: Serbia's Student List runs chemistry professor Radomir Saicic for president
events.summary: After ousting strongman Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia's student movement has now nominated academic Radomir Saicic for the upcoming presidential vote. Saicic accused the "outgoing regime" of trying to collapse the state.

events.title: Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong
events.summary: The tiny Vallarta mud turtle was only discovered in 2018. It's critically endangered with around 300 thought to live in the wild. Almost one tenth of that number were stashed in a traveler's luggage, bound in duct tape.

events.title: Arsenic in the water: Thailand presses Myanmar over mining pollution
events.summary: Thailand is seeking to tackle river pollution stemming from rare earth mines in neighboring Myanmar. The two countries held joint talks this week as a "first step towards agreeing on the evidence."

events.title: Georgia: Police clash with Besiktas fans at Israel club game
events.summary: Turkey's Besiktas accused Georgian police of using "disproportionate" force during the game with Israel's Hapoel Beer-Sheva, which saw Besiktas fans unfurl a banner supporting Palestine.

events.title: Airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, succumbing to aviation fuel costs
events.summary: The low-cost airline was only founded a few years ago and had been struggling to turn a profit. The spike in aviation fuel prices caused by the war in Iran has now driven Norway's Norse Atlantic into bankruptcy.

events.title: As Gambia gears up for election, can Barrow secure a third term?
events.summary: President Adama Barrow is seeking a third term as Gambians vote on December 5. The election will test the opposition's appeal and the country's progress on democratic reform.

events.title: Informer TV owner Vucicevic arrested: Has the reckoning with Serbia's pro-Vucic media machine begun?
events.summary: The arrest of media owner Dragan J. Vucicevic raises questions about whether Serbia is holding the people behind the country's pro-Vucic media accountable — or whether this is another political power struggle.

events.title: BSW set to play major role in German politics once more
events.summary: Sahra Wagenknecht's BSW party is set to disrupt German politics yet again. Espousing a mix of left-wing economic policy and populist far-right anti-migration rhetoric, it now stands to play kingmaker to the far right AfD

events.title: Russia sports ban: Ukraine's Heraskevych hails EU pushback
events.summary: As European countries challenge Russia's sporting return, Ukrainian Olympian Vladyslav Heraskevych believes the IOC is facing a "very big crisis."

events.title: How East Germany boosted Vietnam's coffee industry
events.summary: When East Germany could no longer afford to import coffee, it introduced a substitute blend containing rye and chicory in 1977. A public outcry ensued. The solution to the problem lay 9,000 kilometers away — in Vietnam.

events.title: AI goes from math dunce to genius
events.summary: It once struggled to get simple sums right. But AI is now tackling tough mathematical problems like the Riemann hypothesis. How AI made this extraordinary leap — and why mathematicians should be "deeply worried."

events.title: German Catholic Church abuse victims may receive higher compensation
events.summary: In a landmark ruling, judges in Cologne found the Catholic Church responsible for abuse committed by clergy members. Victims could now be entitled to more compensation.

events.title: Albania's youth are protesting, no longer leaving the country
events.summary: Youth protests against a rigid political system and corruption have shaken the government of Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama. They also show that fewer young people are willing to emigrate in search of a better future.

events.title: Trial of Berlin woman accused of spying for Russia begins after delay
events.summary: Despite delays due to health issues, the trial of the Berlin woman accused of spying for Russia has begun. Prosecutors say the defendant used her military contacts to provide information on German defense and Ukraine.

events.title: On farewell trip, Steinmeier calls for more investment in Africa
events.summary: Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Kenya: On his last trip to Africa, outgoing German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier called on companies at home to be bolder and seize opportunities in Africa.

events.title: Freigang banned — Germany star to miss 2027 World Cup
events.summary: Germany forward Laura Freigang has been suspended until October 2027 after missing three doping tests, ruling her out of next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil. Freigang has denied any intention to evade controls.

events.title: FIFA says a cyberattack against it targeted a 'limited set of personal and business information'
events.summary: World football's governing body says the cyberattack targeted personal and business information. They struck at a sensitive time for the under-fire organization and its president, Gianni Infantino.

events.title: EU-Indonesia trade deal opens new markets, but challenges remain
events.summary: The agreement offers new export and investment opportunities for Jakarta and Brussels. But can Indonesia turn Europe's growing interest in its markets and critical minerals into sustainable gains at home?

events.title: Joshua Kimmich critcizes Bayern bosses over Musiala health comments
events.summary: Joshua Kimmich has slammed Bayern Munich's leadership over comments about Jamal Musiala's health issues. The bosses have questioned whether the player can return to previous form – and is still worth his high salary.

events.title: Crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza coast
events.summary: Authorities rescued 17 crew members but one later died in hospital after a diesel tanker capsized off the Spanish island of Ibiza. A contingency plan against possible pollution damage is now in place.

events.title: Germany news: Cologne court awards record damages in Catholic sex abuse case
events.summary: A court has awarded the highest damages ever in Germany to a victim of sexual abuse linked to the Catholic Church. An alleged spy and suspected terrorists are also making headlines in Germany on Thursday.

events.title: Germany: 2 arrested, suspected of plotting synagogue attack
events.summary: Federal prosecutors say they have ordered the arrest of two members of a pro-Iranian group on suspicion of planning an attack on a synagogue. They were detained in the cities of Heidelberg and Cologne.

events.title: Russia-Ukraine war extends to Baltic, Mediterranean
events.summary: By attacking Russian vessels around the world, Ukraine is trying to increase the pressure on Russia and also sending out signals to its Western allies. What is the impact on global maritime trade?

events.title: Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?
events.summary: SpaceX's US Starlink satellite system has played a key role in countering the Russian military in Ukraine, but now a Russian counterpart is under development. What could this mean for Ukraine?

events.title: Peter Magyar meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Viktor Orban era
events.summary: After years of frosty and hostile relations under Hungary's Kremlin-friendly former PM Viktor Orban, his successor, Peter Magyar, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy seek to reset their countries' ties.

events.title: €561 Billion and Still Not Enough: Germany's 2027 Budget Exposes a Coalition on the Brink
events.summary: The budget for 2027 has reached new highs, and pension funds, defense spending and a weak economy are increasing the pressure. At the same time, tensions are mounting within the government.

events.title: German firms eye Africa as global trade shocks hit traditional markets
events.summary: German businesses are optimistic about Africa, but Berlin's cautious approach to risk is holding them back from cashing in on the opportunities that their competitors from countries like the UAE and Turkey are seizing.

events.title: Ice hockey prospect Max Calce follows Leon Draisaitl's path, leaving Mannheim for Canada
events.summary: The player widely seen as Germany's biggest ice hockey talent to come along in years is leaving the country's top professional league for Canada – changing tracks in his bid to make it to the NHL.

events.title: Climate loss and damage fund exists, but the money doesn't
events.summary: Climate-vulnerable countries fought for years to create a loss and damage fund. Four years on, demand far outstrips funding, pledges are scarce, and disaster-hit nations are still waiting for support.

events.title: Germany's women's football team take stand against domestic violence
events.summary: Germany's women's football team are to wear UN Women badges in games against Argentina and Peru, as domestic violence hits a record high in Germany.

events.title: German auto workers on back foot as costs, competition bite
events.summary: German auto workers profited during the industry's boom years, but are now increasingly being asked to trade past gains for future job security.

events.title: Domestic violence soars to record high in Germany
events.summary: Every three days in Germany, a man kills his wife or ex-partner. Every 10 minutes, the police record a sexual offense against a woman. "A shocking finding," according to Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig.

events.title: Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remains controversial
events.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

events.title: EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?
events.summary: Individual EU member states use their veto powers to block candidate countries in the accession process — often for reasons of domestic politics. DW takes a look at some cases and examines what's behind them.

events.title: CAS reinstates Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions
events.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has reinstated Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions, overturning a CAF decision that stripped them of the title. Morocco, previously declared winners, are confirmed runners-up.

events.title: Bombed factories, billion-dollar opportunity: Why German companies are staying in Ukraine
events.summary: German companies remain committed to Ukraine despite million-dollar losses, an unreliable energy supply and a shortage of skilled workers. They are betting on new markets and long-term growth.

events.title: How cautious investors are struggling to avoid the AI bubble
events.summary: From Nvidia to Coreweave, AI and tech stocks have swung sharply in recent months. Some investors still see plenty of room to run, while others are trying to diversify — and finding it harder than expected.

events.title: German directors' doc on stolen film wins International Emmy Award
events.summary: Two German film students confronted the American who won festival prizes with their animated movie. "The Talented Mr. F," their documentary on their fight against plagiarism, is now in the spotlight.

events.title: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?
events.summary: Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, but satellites are more exposed. We explain how radiation could damage them, why the effects can linger and what protection is possible.

events.title: Weapons, war and wavering trust: Germans want to see more restraint in foreign policy
events.summary: According to a study by the Körber Foundation, a growing number of Germans now oppose providing military aid to Ukraine. The majority also believes that Germany should take a neutral position between the US and China.

events.title: US and UK to host Women's World Cups in 2031 and 2035
events.summary: FIFA has confirmed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host the 2031 Women's World Cup — the first to feature 48 teams. The UK will stage the 2035 edition, its first World Cup since 1966.

events.title: Gukesh to defend chess crown against rising star Sindarov
events.summary: As the World Chess championship gets underway, it's no coincidence that the titleholder, Gukesh Dommaraju, and his challenger, Jakhovir Sindarov, are both from Asia.

events.title: Nvidia reinstates former CEO Jensen Huang despite China espionage scandal
events.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring back the disgraced CEO, who resigned this month amid news of his affairs. He's suspected of having had a relationship with a Chinese intelligence asset.

events.title: North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate
events.summary: EU enlargement has regained momentum, with Montenegro and Albania moving closer to membership. But North Macedonia, a candidate since 2005, remains stalled by a politically difficult dispute involving Bulgaria.

events.title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
events.summary: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.

events.title: COP deadlock prompts calls for a reset of climate diplomacy
events.summary: COP31 has been branded a failure after countries couldn't reach a final agreement, divided over a reference to "fossil fuels." But was the decision to walk away from a watered-down text actually a show of strength?

events.title: German police respond to multiple school bomb threats
events.summary: Police in Germany are responding to bomb threats against a series of schools, but say that at present they don't believe them to be credible. Danish authorities are reporting a similar series of apparent hoaxes.

events.title: 'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract
events.summary: For decades, Germans have known Hollywood's biggest stars through the same familiar voices. Now an AI clause in Netflix contracts is splitting the industry over whether it protects performers or exposes them.

events.title: Budget cuts threaten Germany's fight against antisemitism and racism
events.summary: Numerous grassroots initiatives in Germany are facing funding cuts. Affected organizations are sounding the alarm, pointing to growing challenges posed by far-right extremism.

events.title: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect
events.summary: A new project and exhibition, "The Night Watch Lives," lifts the veil on the hidden world of microbes covering one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.

events.title: Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?
events.summary: Germany plans to pay €10 a month into investment accounts for children to encourage long-term retirement saving. Economists say the measure may help build wealth but won't solve the country's pension funding challenge.

events.title: Germany news: Metalworkers go on strike as pay dispute heats up
events.summary: Germany's biggest union is calling for more strikes over heated pay disputes with car makers like Mercedes and shipyards among the companies impacted. Meanwhile, a Berlin hospital fire leaves many injured.

events.title: Rule-breaking is contagious — and good examples barely help
events.summary: Seeing someone break a rule makes people more likely to break it too, a new study has found, especially when the rule-breaker is on their side politically. Watching others behave well barely made a difference.

events.title: COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use
events.summary: After two weeks of tough talks, the COP31 climate summit has closed without a consensus on how to quit fossil fuels or fund countries struggling to adapt to a hotter world.

events.title: Inspired by Bernie Sanders: A German agency is using US-Style campaigning to boost the left in 2029
events.summary: "The Goodforces" wants to see a swing to the left in the 2029 German elections. The agency counts New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Bernie Sanders among its inspirations. Could it transform the political landscape?

events.title: Germany news: IG Metall union calls for new 24-hour strike
events.summary: Germany's biggest single union, IG Metall, is calling on car and shipyard workers to strike amid a pay row. Meanwhile, Germany's president is setting off on an Africa trip. DW has more.

events.title: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace
events.summary: Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.

events.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
events.summary: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.

events.title: EU takes aim at tech giants in tax proposal
events.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.

events.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
events.summary: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

events.title: Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad
events.summary: Harassment, persecution, surveillance: Across much of the world, people of faith are facing growing pressure. A new German government report is unusually direct in criticizing China in particular.

events.title: Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
events.summary: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.

events.title: COP31: No agreement on climate science, disinformation spreading
events.summary: Attacks on climate science and disinformation risk delaying key measures at COP31 in Antalya. As the UN climate talks draw to a close, how will that affect efforts to come to an agreement?

events.title: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment
events.summary: The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.

events.title: Better educated than ever — yet Germany's Gen Z is being shut out of its own future
events.summary: Never before have young people around the world been so well-educated while facing so many economic challenges. Young Germans are asking: Will I be better off than my parents?

events.title: Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience
events.summary: The US is now officially a measles contagion zone. By mid-2026, there were more infections than in all of the previous year. But the country could beat measles again, just like Brazil did two years ago.

events.title: Germany face Belgium in Nations League quarterfinals — Klopp plays down favorites tag
events.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is looking to "carry positive momentum forward" as his team draw neighboring Belgium in the quarterfinals of the UEFA Nations League.

events.title: EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
events.summary: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.

events.title: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
events.summary: In the latest in a series of raids and arrests, another major pro-opposition Turkish broadcaster has been brought under state control. This is the third in a year.

events.title: FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?
events.summary: Two challengers to Gianni Infantino have registered for next year's FIFA presidential election. What do Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima stand for – and do they stand a chance against the incumbent?

events.title: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs, citing ongoing losses — reports
events.summary: According to a letter obtained by the media, Lufthansa's executive board said the German company is losing €20 million every month. In addition to job cuts, operational cuts are also planned.

events.title: Have we missed our chance to stop climate change?
events.summary: From record-breaking heat to devastating floods and wildfires, the warning signs are everywhere. Can rising temperatures still be brought under control?

events.title: Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?
events.summary: Russian President Putin has suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. But experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?

events.title: No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
events.summary: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas. Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.

events.title: Anthropic trading tests investors' appetite for AI
events.summary: Anthropic was valued at $2 trillion after shares started trading on the Nasdaq following a record $81 billion IPO. Its performance will put investor confidence in AI to the test.

events.title: Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend
events.summary: World No. 1 tennis player Alexander Zverev is facing a new lawsuit related to a domestic abuse trial. The lawyer for his ex-girlfriend, Brenda Patea, told DW what the allegations are against the German player.

events.title: EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
events.summary: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

events.title: Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
events.summary: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

events.title: Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure
events.summary: As Donald Trump seeks to tighten economic pressure on Iran, China remains its biggest oil customer and Russia a key partner. But both powers are balancing support for Tehran against broader interests with Washington.

events.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
events.summary: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

events.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
events.summary: Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with politics and fan culture.

events.title: 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: Europe remains committed to Ukraine
events.summary: The "Coalition of the Willing" supporting Ukraine is gathering in Berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the country's future.

events.title: How a green economy could help reverse climate change
events.summary: Green growth promises a future in which economies thrive without destroying the environment. But is this vision realistic?

events.title: Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair
events.summary: Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.

events.title: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future
events.summary: Germany's fall from grace in recent years has seen the team drift away from the fans. But Monday's drubbing of the Netherlands and the impact of Jürgen Klopp, Florian Wirtz and emerging youngsters offers hope.

events.title: Could the Airbus €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?
events.summary: The US says a record €3 billion financing package for Airbus may conflict with a transatlantic aircraft-subsidy truce. EU officials insist the funding complies with market-based rules.

events.title: Germany news: Plans for Rwanda migrant hub come under fire
events.summary: Human rights groups have slammed plans by Germany and four other EU states to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. In other news, business start-ups in Germany are on track to reach the highest level since 2015.

events.title: France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
events.summary: Philippe Diallo is the second candidate to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino. He is backed by European football's governing body UEFA, known to be critical of Infantino.

events.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth
events.summary: When just saying 'hello' takes a two-day round trip, you're a light-day, or 26 billion kilometers, from Earth. Only one human-made object has ever traveled that far — and its journey into interstellar space continues.

events.title: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades
events.summary: In 1962, a martini-drinking womanizer saved the world for the first time in "Dr. No." As Robert Pattinson takes on the role of 007, here's how the films evolved.

events.title: COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels
events.summary: The preliminary agreement at UN climate talks in Turkey calls for a rapid reduction of planet-warming emissions and at least $120 billion to help countries adapt to climate change.

events.title: Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms
events.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

events.title: Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?
events.summary: In April, about 60 countries held an unprecedented meeting in Colombia to work out a plan to slowly quit oil, coal and gas. How influential is this coalition at the COP31 climate summit?

events.title: Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany
events.summary: His life is a reflection of contemporary German history, addressed via his songs and sharp wit. At 90, he's as feisty as ever.

events.title: What's going on with the polar vortex?
events.summary: Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?

events.title: Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany
events.summary: Two weeks after the CAS ordered ice hockey's governing body to reintegrate Russia into international play, a solution remains elusive. Now Russia has threatened to take legal action against two tournament hosts.

events.title: Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration
events.summary: Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp has said midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in the Nations League.

events.title: Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?
events.summary: The TFFF rainforest fund aims to make forest conservation more profitable than deforestation. But a lack of money may prevent it from getting off the ground.

events.title: Iranian activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi shares her story in memoir
events.summary: Written and smuggled out of prison, the 2023 Nobel Prize laureate's memoir reveals the cost of defying Iran's regime and fighting for freedom.

events.title: Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO
events.summary: Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia into the world’s dominant AI chipmaker, is stepping down as CEO over extramarital affairs. DW examines how losing its figurehead will affect the firm and the US-China AI race.

events.title: What are fossil fuels?
events.summary: They are in our shampoo bottles, power our cars and heat our homes. But what actually are fossil fuels, and why do they matter?

events.title: Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds
events.summary: Women who scored high on intelligence tests were seen as more hostile by their teammates and got less help, a new study finds. High-scoring men faced no such penalty. Research explains why.

events.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
events.summary: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.

events.title: Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?
events.summary: World leaders warn that geopolitical divisions are distracting from the climate crisis as negotiations focus on clean energy and financing, while Iran calls for compensation for war-related environmental damage.

events.title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
events.summary: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

events.title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
events.summary: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.

events.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
events.summary: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.

events.title: Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future
events.summary: Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.

events.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
events.summary: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.

events.title: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion
events.summary: Felix Nmecha's "Crowns down" celebration has drawn criticism from a Borussia Dortmund fan club, reopening debate over faith, inclusion and religious messaging in football.

events.title: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need
events.summary: From EVs and electric buses on the road, heat pumps warming homes and solar panels powering appliances, the shift to electrifying tech is already in full swing. But what exactly does "electrification" mean?

events.title: Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?
events.summary: The heat is on Australia as chief negotiator at the COP31 UN climate conference to forge a path away from coal and gas, and to protect Pacific neighbors facing rising sea levels.

events.title: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health
events.summary: More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

events.title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
events.summary: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

events.title: Norway's ice hockey team says Russia replacing it at World Juniors
events.summary: The wrangling over Russia's return to international ice hockey continues, with Norway saying it has been kicked out of the next major tournament to accommodate Russia. Switzerland has joined a "boycott."

events.title: 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?
events.summary: Three artists share their thoughts on the reunification of East and West Germany. How do they perceive a shared "we" and what gives them cause for optimism?

events.title: Why Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy matters for AI race
events.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has apologized for an affair with a woman the US believes was spying for China. The story could have profound implications for the world's most valuable company and the global AI race.

events.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
events.summary: Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?

events.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?
events.summary: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

events.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
events.summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

events.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
events.summary: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

events.title: Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response
events.summary: A record heat wave. Five years of drought. A nation under pressure. Germany is running its biggest joint crisis exercise to date to test how authorities would cope with an escalating climate emergency.

events.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
events.summary: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?

events.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
events.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

events.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
events.summary: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

events.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
events.summary: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

events.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
events.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

events.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
events.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

events.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
events.summary: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

events.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
events.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

events.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
events.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

events.title: France holds nationwide protests against violence towards women
events.summary: Estimated 840 million women globally are subjected to violence.

events.title: Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
events.summary: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said Saturday an Israeli strike killed two staff members at a clinic in Gaza, with the Israeli army labelling the pair as Hamas "terrorists". Noga Tarnopolsky is live from Jerusalem.

events.title: Three days in the dark: How prepared are we for the lights to go out?
events.summary: Authorities are urging households to prepare for 72 hours without power, water or internet access as cyberattacks, infrastructure failures and extreme weather expose France and other countries to national security vulnerabilities. The message is of practical resilience, not alarm: modest preparations can help keep people safe when essential services falter – and recent security breaches are sparking a wider reckoning across Europe, including France's presidential campaigns.

events.title: Taiwan holds elections to choose mayors and other local leaders
events.summary: Jan Camenzind Broomby is live from Taipei, Taiwan.

events.title: Europe prepares for a very cold winter as temperatures are expected to drop
events.summary: Daniela Domeisen, associate professor at the University of Lausanne, is our guest.

events.title: Outbreak of diarrhea amongst young children in Gabon, Africa
events.summary: In the Gabonese capital, many babies are being admitted to hospitals in a state of dehydration due to diarrhea. The cause: treatment that is often delayed and inadequate.

events.title: France holds nationwide protests against violence towards women
events.summary: Demonstrations condemning violence against women are set to draw thousands across France on Saturday, with feminist organisations, labour unions, students and Yellow Vest activists expected to take part. The marches come amid a broader wave of social unrest, with cost-of-living protests entering their seventh consecutive week.

events.title: More children reunited with their families amid war in Ukraine
events.summary: Nine ​additional ​children have been reunited with ​their ‌families ⁠amid ‌the war ⁠in Ukraine, bringing the ​total to ‌43 amid an ‌effort ​led by US first lady Melania ​Trump, ​the ​White House ​said on Wednesday.

events.title: War in the Middle East: Surge of violence in occupied West Bank
events.summary: The four Israeli soldiers stepped out of their car in the occupied West Bank, their faces masked, their uniforms unmarked and automatic weapons strapped across their shoulders. They had entered a Palestinian olive grove but, little did they expect, the person there planning to tell them to leave could have once been issuing them orders.

events.title: Taiwan awaits local election results as China watches
events.summary: Taipei Mayor ​Chiang Wan-an ​is leading in the vote count in ​an ‌election ⁠against his opponent Puma ‌Shen, Taiwan media outlets ⁠reported on Saturday.

events.title: Syrian Kurds protest against Baghdad leader's moves to assert central control
events.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is taking bold steps to curb rampant oil smuggling, moves that the US has praised but that risk putting him at odds with Iraq's Kurds and neighbouring Iran.

events.title: What are the main issues driving Spain's national election ?
events.summary: Spain will elect a new government on Sunday in a snap election that could unseat Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. The progressive leader has governed Spain for 8 years, presiding over several crises, years of economic expansion and immigration-led population growth. No issue, however, has affected Spaniards during this time as much as unaffordable housing.

events.title: World Health Organization sounds alarm as measles fight stalls
events.summary: Global measles deaths hit a historic low in 2025, the World Health Organization said on Friday, although millions of children ⁠still missed vaccinations and outbreaks persisted in dozens of countries. The UN health agency estimated 9.8 million measles cases and about 72,000 deaths worldwide in 2025 — down 74% from 37.8 million cases in 2000, with deaths falling roughly 91% from about 769,000.

events.title: Immigration, a key issue in Sunday's Spanish snap election
events.summary: Vox has focused its campaign on immigration, which dominated politics after tens of thousands of migrants streamed into Spain's north African city of Ceuta from Morocco in July.

events.title: Live: Ukraine downs Russian drone with laser technology as Moscow intercepts overnight assault
events.summary: Russia shot down over 1,200 drones targeting Moscow overnight, Russian authorities said Saturday. Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up their attacks using projectiles in recent months, with Ukraine confirming on Friday it had downed a Russian jet-powered drone with laser technology for the first time. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

events.title: Taiwan holds local elections under Beijing's watchful gaze
events.summary: Taiwan is electing local leaders across 22 cities and counties on Saturday amid accusations by Taiwanese authorities of attempts by China to interfere and sow distrust in the island-nation’s electoral system. Chinese authorities reject the allegations.

events.title: Hackers reportedly breach US Air Force cloud platform as Pentagon insists systems are secure
events.summary: Hackers reportedly breached the US Air Force's Cloud One platform late Friday, potentially exposing sensitive military data. The Pentagon did not specifically deny that the system had been accessed, but insists its networks remain secure amid an ongoing spate of cyber-related data incidents.

events.title: S&P revises France's outlook from 'stable' to 'negative'
events.summary: Rating agency S&P revised France’s outlook to "negative" from "stable" on Friday, citing growing budget pressures as weak economic growth and higher interest costs make it harder to reduce the deficit.

events.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo
events.summary: First, Uganda is heading for the exit in eastern DR Congo. Kampala has announced the withdrawal of its troops from a key town in North Kivu, as relations with Kinshasa deteriorate following provocative comments from Uganda's army chief. Then, pregnant women are struggling to cope with extreme heat, while health experts warn of growing risks for unborn babies, from dehydration to premature births. And, after seeking safety, opportunity and a better life, many migrants in South Africa now face hostility, violence and growing exclusion. As anti-immigration sentiment gains ground, the country's promise is fading for those who once saw it as a land of hope.

events.title: Ukraine submits Black Sea ceasefire offer, awaits Russian response
events.summary: ⁠Ukraine ​made a Black Sea ceasefire offer ​to enable food exports and passed the details on to international allies, a senior Ukrainian official said Friday, adding that Kyiv was waiting for a response from Moscow. The announcement came a day after Russia attacked ​two foreign grain carriers near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, according to Ukrainian authorities.

events.title: Spanish elections: 'Right-wing voters extremely mobilised, left-wing voters not mobilised enough'
events.summary: “His main political platform is to say, I am not Sánchez, I am the opposite of Sánchez.” As Spain heads to the polls, what do Alberto Núñez Feijóo's campaign and political career tell us about the kind of prime minister he might become? Javier Carbonell, Policy Analyst at the European Politics and Institutions Programme and lecturer at Sciences Po in Paris, joins Gavin Lee to break down the Popular Party leader's efforts to avoid the mistakes of 2023 and keep right-wing voters mobilised without galvanising the left.

events.title: The End of Spain’s ‘Frankenstein’ Coalition? Presidential Plotting in Paris, Kushner & Kremlin Trap
events.summary:
Catch up with the World This Week with Gavin Lee. In just 45 minutes, make sense of seven extraordinary days in global affairs, as Gavin and his handpicked panel of four leading international correspondents unpack the stories shaping the world — and the questions behind the headlines.
 
This week: Spain’s snap election; the presidential plotting unfolding over lunch at the Brasserie Concorde in Paris; Ukraine, Kushner and the ‘Kremlin Trap’; and the question hanging over Iran: whose side is time on?
 
Joining Gavin are New World Magazine columnist Emma-Kate Symonds; Constant Méheut, The New York Times correspondent in Ukraine; Venetia Rainer, Daily Telegraph Foreign Editor and host of Iran: The Latest; and Sarah Morris, France 24’s correspondent in Spain.

events.title: The AI revolution: Will I lose my job?
events.summary: Have you heard of FOBO? It stands for fear of being obsolete. So as AI spreads, is it going to impact women in the workforce more than men? And are we right to be fearful of becoming obsolete? The International Labour Organization has already found occupations dominated by women are nearly twice as likely to be exposed to job losses thanks to generative AI, compared to those dominated by men.

events.title: Is Spain 'nostalgic' for Franco? Would traditional right PP consider an alliance with far-right Vox?
events.summary: After eight years of socialist-led government, Spain is at a crossroads. Can Pedro Sánchez pull off another electoral comeback, or will the conservative Partido Popular make way for the far right into national government for the first time since the end of Franco's 40-year brutal reign? Just back from Madrid, Richard Werly, Europe correspondent for the Swiss daily Blick, joins Angela Diffley to examine the final days of campaigning and the generational divisions shaping Sunday’s snap elections. The youth are divided between the left and the far-right Vox party. Sánchez, nicknamed the “Teflon politician”, has campaigned heavily on housing and social issues. “We may see an outgoing prime minister performing better than expected,” says Werly.

events.title: Seven students killed and up to 99 injured in explosion near Afghan school
events.summary: Seven students have been killed and up to 99 others injured in an explosion believed to be near a school in Afghanistan, said a Taliban interior ministry spokesperson.

events.title: Doctors Without Borders 'outraged' after staff killed in Gaza
events.summary: A humanitarian medical charity says it is "devastated and outraged" after two civil guards at one of its offices in Gaza were killed in an Israeli strike.

events.title: Amazon staff to strike and rally on busiest weekend of the year
events.summary: Amazon employees around the world are set to stage protests on Black Friday amid claims of unfair pay and oppressive working conditions.

events.title: Witnesses contacted as US probe into World Cup sell-off plan intensifies
events.summary: A planned US congressional investigation into FIFA and Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell-off plans is intensifying with requests to speak to current and former FIFA staff, Sky News understands.

events.title: Driver suspected of causing tanker crash in Egypt that killed 31 detained
events.summary: The driver of a car suspected to have caused a fuel tanker to overturn in Egypt, causing the deaths of 31 people, has been detained.
